title: Language-Specific Gaps in AI Safety Training Datasets

bias_targets.methodology: Conducting a structured comparative audit of 20 multilingual AI safety datasets across language slices (representing low-resource Hausa, mid-resource Swahili, and high-resource French) to assess disparities in data provenance, annotation reliability, artifact accessibility, and harm-taxonomy coverage based on language resource tiers.

Evaluating the provenance and harm taxonomies of safety datasets to determine if they are native-authored and culturally grounded, or if they rely on machine-translation from English, thereby imposing Western/English conceptualizations of harm on African languages.
